subject: MedAlign on‑prem deployment: connectivity, node pools, and archive tiering
messages:
From: Tom Harris <tharris@medalign.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@medalign.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment ask — connectivity & storage questions

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the briefing earlier. We need a concise architecture summary for our on‑prem private deployment so our architects and procurement can align on scope and SOW line items. High level asks:

- Network: we will peer via BGP to a vendor MPLS at our colo and also want an option for a dedicated VPC egress path back to our cloud for backups. Can you confirm typical BGP/eBGP flow and firewall rules you require?
- Node pools: we run a mix of low‑latency inference and occasional heavy retraining. Recommend node sizing for predictable latency and spare capacity?
- Storage tiers: expected hot NVMe for KV cache, blockstore SSD for model artifacts and checkpoints, and an archived object tier for long term retention (7y). How do you recommend encryption-at-rest and key management (we prefer using our HSM)?
- Operational controls: audit logging, token redaction, snapshot cadence, and acceptable RTO/RPO for your typical private installs.

Can you provide a doc with recommended node counts (HA considerations), storage classes, and a simple network diagram? We’d like to review internally and get back to procurement by May 10.

If useful, we can set a 30‑minute preflight call — we have availability Fri 11am PT.

Thanks,
Tom Harris
VP Infrastructure, MedAlign
(tharris@medalign.com)


From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Harris <tharris@medalign.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment ask — connectivity & storage questions

Tom — thanks, this is straightforward. I put together an initial architecture summary and attached a one‑page draft (medalign-onprem-arch-draft.pdf). Key recommendations below — high level so legal/ops/procurement can map to SOW items:

1) Cluster footprint and HA
- Control plane: dedicated 3‑node control plane (external etcd, OOB management VLAN) for HA and clear isolation from tenant workloads.
- Worker node pools: 
  - gpu-inference: 3 nodes (N+1) with 2 x A100 each for low‑latency model serving; use fixed instance sizes to preserve predictability.
  - gpu-training (optional burst): 2 nodes, preemptible/standby for scheduled training windows.
  - cpu-serve: 4 nodes (mixture of 32–64 vCPU) for routable web workers + small batch jobs.
  - infra-system: 2 dedicated nodes for monitoring, logging, and ingress proxies (tolerations).
- Pod disruption: set PDBs for critical services (ingress, registry, redis) to preserve steady state.

2) Storage tiering
- Local NVMe: ephemeral local SSD for KV cache and model shards that benefit from ultra-low latency. Recommend using a local CSI plugin exposing per-node NVMe as ephemeral PV; replicate hot cache across nodes at application level.
- Blockstore (CSI → SAN or local NVMe-backed block): for model artifacts, container images, and checkpoints. Use a standard RWX/RWO mix, snapshot schedule nightly with 7‑day rolling backups to object tier.
- Object archive: S3-compatible object storage (on‑site or cloud tunnel) for retention (7 years). Encrypt objects using customer KMS (see KMS section).

3) Encryption & KMS
- Envelope encryption: Redwood supports using customer‑managed keys (external HSM/KMS) via envelope encryption. We recommend customer KMS for key rotation and auditability.
- Disk-level: mount blockstore with LUKS or storage backend encryption depending on hardware; ensure passphrases are backed by customer KMS and rotated per policy.

4) Network & BGP
- BGP peering: we expect eBGP sessions with your colo router. Typical configuration: two BGP sessions (primary/backup), advertise /24s for node egress pools and accept routes for service VIPs.
- NAT & egress: use a dedicated NAT gateway cluster in the VPC for cloud egress backups; for colo-only installs, we place NAT on a pair of edge routers with failover.
- Firewall rules: allow 6443 (kube API) from management CIDRs only, 10250 (kubelet) between nodes, ports 80/443 for ingress, and ephemeral ports for inter-pod comms. We'll supply a minimal ACL template.

5) Observability & Compliance
- Audit logs: Kubernetes audit logs forwarded to your SIEM (TLS to syslog endpoint) with token redaction.
- Tracing/metrics: Prometheus + Grafana in infra-system nodes with metrics retention policy (30d by default; extended retention available as add‑on).
- RTO/RPO: default RTO 2 hours for control-plane critical failures (with Dedicated SLA), RPO depends on snapshot cadence — we recommend nightly snapshots with object replication for retention-critical data.

Next steps: I’ll pull in network and infra specifics from Irene and Karthik below to finalize the diagram and PV sizing. If this looks acceptable you can share the attached draft with procurement — I flagged KMS and HA items as negotiable line items.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
+1 415 555 0143

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Tom Harris <tharris@medalign.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment ask — connectivity & storage questions

Laura / Tom — quick technical clarifications from network and operations side. Adding these will avoid surprises during on‑site prep: 

- CNI & IP addressing: we recommend Calico in policy-only mode with BGP peering disabled in CNI; Redwood will rely on layer‑3 routing from the fabric and advertise node ranges via edge routers. Allocate a /21 for pods and a /24 per nodepair for host IPs to keep ARP tables sane.
- MTU: set MTU 8900 across the fabric if using jumbo frames (recommended for NVMe over Fabrics). Confirm with colo if switches support it.
- Masking & SNAT: prefer no masquerade for intra‑cluster traffic; SNAT only at egress NAT for cloud backups. This preserves source IPs for policy enforcement.
- Ingress: we suggest Envoy (edge) with TLS termination at the ingress cluster, and re‑encrypt to services where required. Could use existing customer load balancers if you have external VIPs.
- Management plane access: OOB management VLAN with jump host; no direct public kube-api access. We’ll provide an SSH bastion playbook for imaging.

Operational notes:
- Node imaging: we typically ship a pre-built OS/agent image. On‑site imaging window ~4 hours per rack (including BIOS/KMS enrollment).
- Backups: we support streaming snapshots to an S3 endpoint (site→cloud) or to your on‑prem object store via TLS. Please confirm throughput allowed on your uplink for nightly snapshot windows.

I attached a small spreadsheet (kv-cache-ops.xlsx) showing recommended local NVMe sizing per node based on expected cache footprint and eviction policy.

- Irene
Irene Choi | Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Harris <tharris@medalign.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment ask — connectivity & storage questions

Thanks — a few storage and sizing confirmations from my side before we finalize the SOW:

- GPU sizing: the proposed 3 x A100 nodes in gpu-inference (N+1) is the right balance for targeted p95 latency SLAs with 2 replicas per model. For heavier throughput windows we can configure autoscale policies tied to queue depth.
- KV cache durability: local NVMe with application-level replication is best for latency. Add a nightly checkpoint push to object archive so cold restarts don’t require warm-up traffic. We suggest a lightweight KV snapshot every 6 hours and a full push nightly. See kv-cache-ops.xlsx for numbers.
- PV classes: define 3 storage classes: local-nvme (ephemeral, RWO), fast-block (provisioned IOPS, RWO), archive-object (S3, OBJECT). Set reclaimPolicy=Retain for fast-block so model artifacts survive node drains until snapshot completes.
- Eviction/QoS: mark critical pods Guaranteed/QoS where possible; use PDBs to avoid disrupting replicas during maintenance.

I’ll add a short data‑flow diagram to the Drive link and ask Legal to include an architecture exhibit for KMS and data movement in the contract.

I can present these notes at your Fri preflight call if you confirm the time.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Ops Architect, Redwood Inference
